name: Teal Blue
lede: Teal Blue is a moderate greenish blue named for the dark patch on the wings of the teal duck; it is a softer, greyer color than the web-standard teal.

sections.title: A duck's wing
sections.body:
Paterson defines teal as the dark greenish-blue color found on the wings of the teal, a small duck, and notes that it is also called teal blue [1].

Online, teal means something sharper. The X11 color set defines Teal as #008080, a saturated cyan-green, and this swatch is a different color, a duller, greyer blue [1][2]. The 2010 xkcd survey gave another teal-like color, #01889F, so even the crowd did not agree [2]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system files this swatch under "moderate greenish blue", only 1.7 CIEDE2000 units away, a close fit [2].

The record for teal blue in the Maerz and Paul dictionary is at plate 39, block L 6, with a first recorded use of 1927 [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Teal Blue is uncommon in painting [3]. It appears in 100 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, 0.42 per cent, rarer than 56 per cent of the named colors [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, in 45 per cent of the 33 paintings where the within-painting lens finds it [3]. It peaks in the 1700s, at 0.2 per cent of the 3,449 paintings from that century, 1.5 times the museums' baseline [3].

The earliest dated match is 1433, a Robert Campin, 497 years before the name's first record in our sources, and the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is a look-alike hue and not proof of a pigment [3]. In printed English the words peak in the 2010s and rose fastest in the 1980s [4].
